To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the single 2,3-dehydroquinaldate dehydratase of the quinate degrading actinomycetes Amycolatopsis is a bifunctional enzyme involved in the biosynthesis of phenylalanine and tyrosine and the catabolization of quinate.

the single 2-keto-3-deoxy-4-hydroxy-5-oxocyclohexane-1-carboxylate aldolase present in Amycolatopsis sp. strain M497 is involved both in the biosynthesis of the aromatic amino acids (as a shikimate pathway enzyme) and the catabolization of quinate (as a 3-deoxyquinate dehydrase).
a 3-deydroquinate dehydrase with dual function in the biosynthesis and catabolism was found in the actinomyce Amycolatopsis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the catabolic quinate pathway in the actinomycte Amycolatopsis (Streptomyces) methanolica, and the elucidation of its regulation and genetics.
the characterization of the quinate/shikinate dehydrogenase and the 3-dehydroquinase dehydratase in A. methanolicus.
the elucidation of the quinate catabolic pathway in Amycolatopsis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dual function 3-DHQA dehydratase of A. methanolicum is the first example of an enzyme involved in both catabolic and anabolic metabolism of aromatic compounds.
A. methanolicas 3-dehydroquinase is an unusual enzyme which is a dual function protein.
the 3-dehydroquinase from A. methanolicas has been purified, characterized and found to be a dual function enzyme.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 3-dehydroquinates synthase and dehydratase genes of A. methanolicus are linked but transcribed separately, and that 3-dehydroqinate dehydratases of this type are dual function enzymes.
A. methanolida has evolved an unusual metabolic pathway for the catabolization of quinate.
the dual function 3-DHQ dehydratase of Amycolatopsis has been purified to homogeneity, and its molecular and kinetic properties have been characterized.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the quinate degradative pathway in A. methanolicus is more complex than previously believed.
the quinate catabolism pathway in A. metholica is a hybrid pathway in which the 3-dehydroquinic acid dehydratase is bifunctional and the 3-dehydroschikimic acid dehydrase is absent.

the quinate catabolism pathway is more widespread than previously thought, and that the 3-dehydroquinase enzyme is a dual function enzyme involved in both quinate catabolic and shikimate biosynthetic pathways.
